From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: security follow-ups and next steps

Hi Lisa - great to meet today, and thanks for walking Tom and the security team through the demo. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a Type II SOC 2 report (last assessment: Q4 2026). I can share the redacted report and the test-of-controls summary.
- Subprocessors: Per your ask, I will share our current subprocessor list with cloud provider details and processing boundaries.
- Vendor questionnaire: happy to start the standard security questionnaire - do you prefer a spreadsheet (XLSX) or an online portal?
- Data boundaries: we scoped the demo to inference-only (no long-term storage of customer prompts by default). We can send the data flow diagram and retention settings.

Action items:
1) I will attach the subprocessor CSV and link to the SOC 2 report by EOD Monday.
2) Please send the vendor questionnaire format and any specific encryption/KMS questions you want highlighted.
3) If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min session with our security engineering manager (David) next week.

Thanks again - next step: I'll send the attachments and a short note with answers to your outstanding security questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[Attachment stub will be included in follow-up]

Thanks Marissa - that summary is perfect. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SOC 2: we'll need the Type II report and the bridge letter (if available). Redacted copies are fine.
2) Subprocessors: please include cloud provider(s) (region-level info if possible), any CDN or logging providers, and whether any subprocessors have access to PII.
3) Data boundaries: can you confirm whether prompt data is stored for more than 30 days by default for debugging or tooling? Also confirm options for disabling retention.
4) Vendor questionnaire: XLSX is best for our intake team - I'll attach our standard security spreadsheet in a follow-up email.

If you can get the subprocessor list and SOC 2 link by Monday, we can route to procurement and security for an initial review.

Appreciate it - Lisa
Lisa Chen

lisa.chen@acmecorp.com

Hi Lisa - attaching the subprocessor list and SOC 2 link as promised. See highlights below, and I included the full CSV for your intake team.

Key points (summary):
- SOC 2 Type II (period: Nov 2025 - Oct 2026). Redacted report: https://redwood-share.example.com/soc2/2026-report
- Subprocessors attached: redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv (columns: name, role, region, access_type, contract_reviews, pci/hipaa scope)
- Cloud providers: Primary compute for inference: AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1) and GCP (us-central1) as fallback. We use S3/GCS for ephemeral object storage (logs & metrics are retained per-customer config).
- PII access: No human access to prompt content as a default. Access is limited to automated logs; debug access is gated and audited (requires formal request).
- Retention: Default short-term retention = 7 days for prompt traces; can be configured to 0 days or turned off per workspace.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv (text/csv)], [Link: https://redwood-share.example.com/soc2/2026-report]

Next steps:
- I'll upload the CSV to the XLSX template once you send it.
- David (cc'd) can join a 30-min review on Wed to go through the access controls and KMS details. Are you available 10-10:30am PT?

If you need a signed subprocessor addendum or data processing agreement redline, we can loop our legal team.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Tom - quick answers below and next steps to lock this down:

- Regional controls: we can restrict processing to US-only regions for your pilot. Primary compute is AWS us-west-2/us-east-1; GCP is configured as a fallback but can be disabled for your account. We will add a regional enforcement flag to your workspace configuration.
- CDN/analytics: the subprocessor list includes FastEdge CDN (edge caching only, logs sent to US region by default) and LogStream Analytics (log aggregation; logs are stored in US buckets unless otherwise requested). Both have contractual EU data handling restrictions and we can mandate US-only for AcmeCorp.
- Next steps:
  1) I'll upload the subprocessor CSV into your XLSX questionnaire once you send it.
  2) David can join a technical call Thursday 7/1 at 10am PT to review KMS and audit logging. Please confirm 7/1 10am PT or propose another slot.
  3) If you require a signed data processing addendum (DPA) with EU data restrictions, we can provide a template and legal contact.

I've attached the CSV again here for convenience.
